narrative_obligations.detail: Trust must change through earned cooperation, not instant friendship.
The compass must ultimately remain lost rather than be replaced by a reward.

artifact.prose:
The brass compass gleamed in the lighthouse nest, close enough for Ekin to imagine its familiar weight in her hand.

“Wait,” Duru said.

Ekin reached for the compass anyway. Duru saw her fingers stretch toward the brass.

The cat-sized hatchling gave a frightened cry and sprang aside. It struck the nest, knocking the compass over the edge. The compass hit the narrow stair and began sliding down, ringing against each step.

“No!” Ekin rushed after it.

The hatchling scrambled down the turning stair ahead of her, unable to fly. Duru followed Ekin close behind. As they reached the dry middle section of the stair, Ekin saw the hatchling flee into the lower room and climb onto a dry ledge.

A heavy scrape sounded above.

The mother sea dragon pushed into the stair after her hatchling, rain running from her scales. She tried to force her body around the narrow turn, but she could not fit. She drew back and tried again. Ekin watched her fail to descend, blocked by the tight bend.

Below, the compass slid off the final step and stopped on the lower floor.

Then the storm struck in full.

A wave burst through the fixed sea-facing iron grate. Water spread across the lower room, cutting the hatchling off on its ledge. The compass spun in the rushing flood.

Ekin took one step down.

“Stay on the dry section!” Duru shouted.

Another surge crashed through the grate. Ekin stopped beside Duru, safely above the floodwater, and watched the compass sweep toward the iron bars.

For one instant, its brass face flashed in the gray water. Then it washed through the grate and vanished into the sea.

Ekin stared after it. Her grandfather’s compass was truly gone.

Below, the uninjured hatchling crouched on the dry ledge while water rose around it. Above, its mother strained helplessly against the stair turn.

Ekin looked at the place where she had reached, then at the danger her impatience had begun. Her hands tightened into fists, but she stayed with Duru on the dry section of the stair.
